question: Who won the 2024 World Series and what was the series score?
answer: Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the New York Yankees 4-1
explanation: 2024 WS at Dodger Stadium/Yankee Stadium; Freddie Freeman won MVP with record-tying 12 RBI.

question: Who holds the MLB single-season home run record and how many did he hit?
answer: Barry Bonds holds the record with 73 home runs in 2001
explanation: AL record is Aaron Judge 62 (2022); Bonds 73 passed McGwire's 70 (1998).

question: How many strikes are required for a strikeout under MLB rules?
answer: 3 strikes
explanation: A batter is out after three strikes; a foul with two strikes is not a third strike except bunt.

question: What is the nickname of the 37-foot left-field wall at Fenway Park, home of the Boston Red Sox?
answer: The Green Monster
explanation: 37'2" high, 231 ft to left field line; built 1934, painted green in 1947.

question: Who is the captain of the New York Yankees as of the 2025 season and what position does he play?
answer: Aaron Judge — captain and right fielder (also DH) for the Yankees since December 2022
explanation: Named 16th Yankees captain after re-signing 9yr/$360M in Dec 2022.

question: What contract did Juan Soto sign before the 2025 season and with which team?
answer: 15-year, $765 million contract with the New York Mets (signed December 2024, largest in professional sports history)
explanation: Opt-out after 2029; surpassed Ohtani's $700M (with deferrals) as largest present-day value.

question: Which of these teams returned to the postseason in 2024 after a 10-year drought by going 86-76 as a Wild Card: Detroit Tigers, and who did they beat in the Wild Card Series?
answer: Detroit Tigers went 86-76 and swept the Houston Astros 2-0 in the AL Wild Card Series
explanation: Tigers won 31 of last 44 to clinch; Tarik Skubal started Game 1.

question: Which Texas Rangers rookie hit for the cycle on June 30, 2024, against the Baltimore Orioles, becoming the first Rangers rookie to do so?
answer: Wyatt Langford hit for the cycle on June 30, 2024 vs the Baltimore Orioles
explanation: At Globe Life Field; 4-for-5 with 1B, 2B, 3B, HR.

question: Who is the longtime center fielder for the Los Angeles Angels who has won 3 American League MVP awards (2014, 2016, 2019) and is widely regarded as the best player of the 2010s?
answer: Mike Trout — center fielder for the Los Angeles Angels, 3-time AL MVP (2014, 2016, 2019)
explanation: Trout debuted 2011, 11x All-Star, also 2012 ROY; injuries limited him 2021-24 but still active in 2025.

question: What position does Gunnar Henderson play for the Baltimore Orioles and what award did he win in 2023?
answer: Shortstop (and third base) — won 2023 American League Rookie of the Year
alternates: Henderson shortstop Rookie of the Year
explanation: Henderson hit 28 HR in 2023; also 2024 All-Star, Silver Slugger.

question: Which franchise is second to the Yankees in World Series titles with 11 championships, most recently in 2011?
answer: St. Louis Cardinals with 11 World Series titles (last in 2011 vs Texas Rangers)
explanation: Cards beat Rangers 4-3 in 2011; David Freese WS MVP.

question: Under current MLB pitch clock rules (as of 2024), how many seconds does a pitcher have to begin his delivery with the bases empty versus with runners on?
answer: 15 seconds with bases empty, 18 seconds with runners on (reduced from 20 in 2023)
explanation: 2024 reduction from 20 to 18 with runners; violations are automatic balls.

question: Which ballpark is known as the most hitter-friendly in MLB due to its mile-high altitude (5,280 feet) in Denver?
answer: Coors Field, home of the Colorado Rockies
explanation: Altitude lowers air density; humidor installed 2002 to normalize scoring.

question: Which star closer was traded from the Milwaukee Brewers to the San Diego Padres at the 2022 trade deadline on August 1, 2022?
answer: Josh Hader was traded from the Brewers to the Padres on August 1, 2022
explanation: Return included Taylor Rogers, Dinelson Lamet, Esteury Ruiz, Robert Gasser.

question: Which ballpark, home to the Pittsburgh Pirates, is located on the Allegheny River and is consistently ranked as one of MLB's most beautiful stadiums?
answer: PNC Park in Pittsburgh
explanation: Opened 2001; view of Roberto Clemente Bridge and downtown skyline.

question: Who set the MLB single-season hits record with 262 hits in 2004 and which team was he on?
answer: Ichiro Suzuki set the record with 262 hits in 2004 for the Seattle Mariners
explanation: Broke George Sisler's 1920 record of 257; also holds professional hits record (4,367 including NPB).

question: Which team ended a 108-year World Series drought by beating the Cleveland Indians 4-3 in the 2016 World Series?
answer: Chicago Cubs beat the Cleveland Indians 4-3 in the 2016 World Series
explanation: Cubs trailed 3-1, forced Game 7, Rajai Davis HR, Ben Zobrist MVP.

question: Which flamethrowing reliever represented the Athletics (still listed as Oakland Athletics in 2024) as their lone All-Star on the 2024 AL roster?
answer: Mason Miller — Athletics closer, 2024 AL All-Star
explanation: Miller threw 103.6 mph in All-Star Game; 28 saves in 2024 despite team record.

question: Who is the star third baseman for the Cleveland Guardians known for his switch-hitting and multiple All-Star selections, who signed a 7-year extension in 2022?
answer: José Ramírez — third baseman for the Cleveland Guardians, 7yr/$141M extension in 2022
explanation: 6x All-Star, 4x Silver Slugger; has played entire career with Cleveland since 2013.

question: How many outs are there per half-inning in a regulation MLB game?
answer: 3 outs per half-inning
explanation: Three outs end the offensive half; 6 outs per full inning, 27 outs per 9-inning regulation game per team.

question: Who holds the MLB career stolen base record and how many did he steal?
answer: Rickey Henderson holds the career record with 1,406 stolen bases
explanation: Lou Brock was previous record holder with 938; Henderson also holds single-season record 130 (1982).

question: Who became the first player to achieve a 40 home run / 70 stolen base season in 2023 and what were his exact totals?
answer: Ronald Acuña Jr. of the Atlanta Braves — 41 HR and 73 SB in 2023, also first 40/70, won NL MVP
explanation: Also created 30/60 club earlier in season; stole 70th on Sept 27.

question: Which ace was traded from the Milwaukee Brewers to the Baltimore Orioles on February 1, 2024?
answer: Corbin Burnes was traded from the Brewers to the Orioles on February 1, 2024
alternates: Corbin Burnes Brewers to Orioles Feb 2024
explanation: Return: DL Hall, Joey Ortiz, 2024 comp pick; Burnes was 2021 NL Cy Young.

question: Which domed ballpark, home to the Tampa Bay Rays since 1998, features catwalks and a fixed roof due to Florida weather?
answer: Tropicana Field (The Trop) in St. Petersburg, home of the Tampa Bay Rays
explanation: Only fixed-roof MLB park from 2020-2024; damaged by Hurricane Milton in Oct 2024 requiring repairs.

question: Which team swept the Houston Astros 4-0 to win the 2005 World Series, ending an 88-year drought?
answer: Chicago White Sox swept the Houston Astros 4-0 in the 2005 World Series
explanation: Jermaine Dye MVP; only White Sox title since 1917.

question: Which team won the National League East in 2024 with a 95-67 record and was the No. 2 seed in the NL?
answer: Philadelphia Phillies won the NL East in 2024 with a 95-67 record
explanation: Lost NLDS 3-1 to Mets despite division title.

question: Which Cincinnati Reds shortstop wears #44 and was the fastest player in MLB in 2024 with 30.2 ft/sec sprint speed and 67 steals?
answer: Elly De La Cruz — Cincinnati Reds SS, #44, 67 stolen bases in 2024
explanation: Debuted June 2023; also hit 25 HR in 2024.

question: Who won 2024 National League Rookie of the Year as a Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher with an 11-3 record and 1.96 ERA after debuting May 11, 2024?
answer: Paul Skenes — Pittsburgh Pirates, 11-3, 1.96 ERA, 2024 NL Rookie of the Year
explanation: LSU product drafted 1-1 in 2023; also started 2024 All-Star Game for NL.

question: What is the distance from the pitcher's rubber to home plate in MLB?
answer: 60 feet, 6 inches
explanation: Measured from front of rubber to back point of home plate; set in 1893.

question: Who led the Kansas City Royals in 2024 with a .332 batting average, 32 home runs, and was the AL MVP runner-up?
answer: Bobby Witt Jr. — .332 AVG, 32 HR, 109 RBI, AL MVP runner-up in 2024
explanation: Also led AL in hits (211); signed 11yr/$288.8M extension Feb 2024.

question: What were the headline terms of Shohei Ohtani's contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers announced in December 2023?
answer: 10-year, $700 million contract with the Dodgers — $680M deferred until after the contract, signed Dec 9, 2023
explanation: Largest guarantee at signing; $68M deferred annually without interest 2034-2043.

question: Which ballpark, home to the Arizona Diamondbacks, features a retractable roof and a swimming pool beyond the outfield fence?
answer: Chase Field in Phoenix — home of the Arizona Diamondbacks, with a pool in right-center
explanation: Opened 1998 as Bank One Ballpark; first MLB park with retractable roof over natural grass.

question: Which Minnesota Twins shortstop was the team's lone position-player All-Star in 2024 despite playing only 86 games?
answer: Carlos Correa made the 2024 AL All-Star team as the Twins' shortstop
explanation: Correa hit .310/.363/.484 before plantar fasciitis; replacement Willi Castro also named.

question: How many World Series championships have the New York Yankees won, and which team is second with 11?
answer: New York Yankees have 27 World Series titles — second is St. Louis Cardinals with 11
explanation: Yankees last won 2009 vs Phillies; 40 AL pennants also most.

question: Which Miami Marlins infielder won the National League batting title in 2023 with a .354 average, then was traded to the Padres in May 2024?
answer: Luis Arraez — won 2023 NL batting title at .354 with Miami Marlins, traded to San Diego Padres May 4, 2024
explanation: Back-to-back batting titles AL 2022 (.316 MIN) and NL 2023; first since DJ LeMahieu.

question: Which Toronto Blue Jays franchise icon and first baseman was their lone 2024 All-Star and hit 30 HR with a .940 OPS in 2024?
answer: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. — Toronto Blue Jays 1B, 2024 AL All-Star, 30 HR
alternates: Vladimir Guerrero Jr Blue Jays 30 HR 2024
explanation: Also won 2021 All-Star Game MVP; son of Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero.

question: What extra-innings rule from 2020 places a runner on second base to start each half-inning in regular-season games, often called the 'ghost runner' or 'Manfred Man'?
answer: The automatic runner (ghost runner / Manfred Man) — runner starts on second base each extra inning
alternates: ghost runner second base extra innings
explanation: Permanent since 2023; not used in postseason.

question: Who holds the career record for no-hitters with 7 and also holds the strikeout record with 5,714?
answer: Nolan Ryan — 7 career no-hitters and 5,714 strikeouts
explanation: No-hitters with Angels (1), Astros (1), Rangers (2) and no-hitters not listed counted; also holds walk record 2,795.

question: Which future Hall of Fame pitcher was traded from the New York Mets back to the Houston Astros at the 2023 deadline on August 1, 2023?
answer: Justin Verlander was traded from the Mets back to the Astros on August 1, 2023
explanation: Mets paid $52.5M of remaining contract; return Drew Gilbert, Ryan Clifford.

question: Which team overcame a 2-0 and 3-2 deficit to beat the Houston Astros 4-3 in the 2019 World Series for their first championship?
answer: Washington Nationals beat the Houston Astros 4-3 in the 2019 World Series
explanation: All 7 games won by road team; Stephen Strasburg WS MVP; Howie Kendrick HR Game 7.
